text:
Alex Gomez: Hey all — quick postmortem doc starter. We saw degraded allocation in eu-west-1 last night (21:34–21:52 UTC). Root cause: subnet IP exhaustion caused the autoscaler to repeatedly fail creating GPU pods, and a warm-pool ordering bug prevented the reserve pool from being used predictably. Impact: ~4% increased p99 latency for hosted API, and a short cost spike as traffic shifted to Dedicated fallback.
Samir Patel: Confirmed. Kube events showed: 

```
Warning  FailedCreate  2m (x5 over 3m)  pod-gpu-autoscaler  failed to create pod: FailedCreatePodSandBox: network plugin error: failed to allocate IP address from range
```

Samir Patel: Autoscaler retried but never got capacity because the AZ subnets were full. The warm-pool instances existed but warm-pool allocator returned them out of order (oldest-first) causing scheduling constraints to fail.
Maria Chen: We also saw fallback routing kick in to another region for a subset of customers. That routing was correct but we didn't have cost-guardrails on the fallback policy so billing jumped. Filed billing spike alert to finance. :grimacing:
OpsBot: Incident 2026-03-18-euw1 created. Severity: S2. Links: https://incidents.redwood/2026/euw1-1958001234
Ryn: Posted logs and timeline in the incident doc. Quick reproduction steps: 
1) Exhaust a /20 subnet by iterating pod creates across AZs.
2) Trigger autoscaler with a burst.
3) Observe IP allocation errors and warm-pool selection log lines.

Commands used: 
```
kubectl get events -n infra | grep FailedCreate
kubectl describe node <node> --show-allocatable
```
Kevin Liu: Working on a small runbook patch now. Proposed edits: add pre-check step to validate subnet free IPs before a large autoscale event; add a sticky warm-pool selection policy (prefer nearest healthy warm instance), and add cost caps when routing to fallback pools. I'll open a PR and link it here.
Alex Gomez: Action items (owner / due): 
- Kevin: PR for runbook edits + patch for warm-pool selection policy (due EOD tomorrow).
- Samir: Add a pre-scale subnet check in autoscaler pipeline + unit test (due 3 days).
- Maria: Add billing alert & set temporary cost cap on eu-west fallback routing (done: note in doc) (follow-up 1 day).
- Ryn: Add a chore to infra backlog to reserve /21 per AZ for critical pools (due 2 weeks).

Samir Patel: For the autoscaler change, plan: run a cheap check before scaling: query IPAM for available IPs in candidate AZs and fail-over to queueing/burst-buffer if < threshold. Pseudocode: 
```
available = ipam.get_free_ips(az)
if available < 50:
  throttle_scale()
else:
  proceed()
```
Samir Patel: Also adding instrumentation metrics: ipam.free_ips_by_az and warmpool.selection_latency.
Maria Chen: Billing note: set fallback-routing max-monthly-cost = $X for now and add a hard webhook to @finance if exceeded. I updated the incident doc with the temporary limit.
Kevin Liu: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/472 — includes runbook text diff and a small helper script to enumerate free IPs: `scripts/ip-check.sh`. Please review.
Ryn: Proposed runbook text snippet to add: 
```
Pre-scale checklist:
- run `scripts/ip-check.sh --az eu-west-1a` and verify > 200 free IPs
- if < 200 free IPs, notify infra-oncall and enable scale-throttle
- if warm-pool present, run `warmpool verify-ordering` and ensure preferred assignment
```
Alex Gomez: Good. Two process changes: 1) Add a mandatory pre-scale check for any manual or scheduled bulk scale. 2) Add a cost-guard checkbox to any cross-region fallback rollout.
OpsBot: Note: oncall rotation change triggered: @Samir moved to primary for eu-west until warmer ordering fix deployed.
Kevin Liu: I'll add a unit test for `warmpool.verify-ordering` and a small e2e that simulates subnet exhaustion so we don't regress.
Alex Gomez: Final owners & next steps: Kevin merge PR and coordinate a canary deploy of warm-pool ordering fix (owner Kevin, due 48h). Samir ship autoscaler pre-check (owner Samir, due 72h). Ryn schedule reservation work and update capacity modeling (owner Ryn, due 2 weeks). Maria confirm cost cap persisted to config and notify finance (owner Maria, due 24h).
Maria Chen: Confirmed cost cap persisted. Pinged finance. :white_check_mark:
Samir Patel: Adding a follow-up to runbook: include snippet to expand /20->/19 with cloud ops approval steps when we see sustained >90% IP utilization for 24h.
Alex Gomez: Thanks all. I'll update the incident doc with the action items and close this thread once PRs land and the warm-pool e2e passes. :thumbsup:
